question: The Hill area development programme was initiated during the ______ th five-year plan.
solution:
The correct answer is __**5th Five-Year Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Hill Area Development Programme** was initiated during the **5th Five-Year Plan** (1974-1979) in India.
 
• The programme was primarily aimed at promoting the **socio-economic development** of hilly regions and addressing challenges specific to these areas, such as infrastructure deficits and ecological fragility.
 
• This plan identified areas that required **special development measures** due to their unique geographical and socio-economic conditions.
 
• The focus of this programme was on **agriculture, horticulture, animal husbandry, forestry, and eco-friendly development** practices.
 
• The programme also emphasized **environmental conservation** and efforts to prevent soil erosion, deforestation, and other ecological issues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **5th Five-Year Plan (1974-1979):**

 
 
• The 5th Five-Year Plan was introduced under the leadership of **Prime Minister Indira Gandhi**.
 
• It focused on achieving **self-reliance** and promoting **poverty alleviation** through programmes like **Garibi Hatao**.
 
• The plan aimed to address regional disparities, including the development of hilly and backward areas.
 
• It was influenced by the global oil crisis of 1973 and emphasized **energy security** and resource optimization.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Hill Areas:**
 
 
• Hilly regions often face challenges such as **poor infrastructure, difficult terrain, ecological fragility, and limited economic opportunities**.
 
• The Hill Area Development Programme aimed to **mitigate these challenges** through targeted investments and development strategies.
 
 
 
• **Focus Areas of the Programme:**
 
 
• Promoting **agriculture and allied activities** like horticulture and animal husbandry.
 
• Strengthening **forestry** and environmental conservation efforts.
 
• Developing **infrastructure**, such as roads, electricity, and water supply systems.
 
• Encouraging **community participation** in development activities.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Programme:**
 
 
• It helped improve the **socio-economic conditions** of people living in hilly regions by creating livelihood opportunities.
 
• Contributed to **environmental conservation** and sustainable development practices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hill Area Development Programme vs Western Ghats Programme:**

 
 
• The Hill Area Development Programme was distinct from the **Western Ghats Programme**, which targeted conservation and development in the Western Ghats region.
 
• Both programmes shared a focus on **ecological sustainability**, but their geographical coverage and objectives differed.
 
 
 
• **Subsequent Plans:**
 
 
• Later Five-Year Plans continued to support hilly regions under various schemes, emphasizing **sustainable development** and **poverty reduction**.
 
• Regional development initiatives like the **Integrated Tribal Development Programmes** also contributed to the welfare of communities in hill areas.
